name: Hodaviah
overview: Hodaviah was a male leader from the tribe of Manasseh, noted in Scripture as a head of households within his tribe. His role indicates a position of responsibility and leadership among the descendants of Manasseh. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodaviah means 'give thanks to YHWH,' reflecting a theocentric dedication common in Hebrew names. This proper name emphasizes gratitude toward God but was not given by divine revelation. It is recorded in 1 Chronicles 5:24.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hodaviah as a descendant of Manasseh, linking him to the tribal lineage of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hodaviah's significance lies in his leadership role as a head of households within the tribe of Manasseh, demonstrating the organizational structure of Israelite tribes during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles. His mention underscores the importance of tribal heads in maintaining order and governance among God's people. This reflects God's providential care in appointing leaders to steward His covenant community.
